requirements.title: The site shall render in dark theme by default, with a control to switch to light theme that persists the visitor's choice

captured_retroactively.reason: Implemented and live-tested against the real second-brain vault during the epic's UX redesign before it had formal TOR coverage; captured now as part of requirements reconciliation.

vision.paraphrase: A dark-first visual presentation with an available light alternative better suits a data-dense graph visualization tool and a job-seeking portfolio site.

requirements.title: The / and /graph pages shall display a header with the product logo and title, and the browser tab title shall reflect the product

captured_retroactively.reason: Implemented and live-tested during the epic's UX redesign before it had formal TOR coverage; captured now as part of requirements reconciliation.

vision.paraphrase: Consistent product branding (logo, title, tab title) across pages signals a finished product rather than an unedited framework scaffold.

requirements.title: The / page shall present a product introduction and call-to-action into /graph instead of the default Next.js starter content

captured_retroactively.reason: Implemented and live-tested during the epic's UX redesign before it had formal TOR coverage; captured now as part of requirements reconciliation.

vision.paraphrase: A visitor landing on the site should immediately understand what the tool does and how to explore it, rather than encountering unedited framework boilerplate.

requirements.title: The / and /graph pages shall render body and heading text in the Geist typeface, never falling back to Arial or a generic sans-serif default

vision.paraphrase: Geist typography actually applied (not falling back to Arial) signals deliberate design and finishes the product aesthetic, fixing issue #4 finding A9.
Deliberate visual identity includes Geist typography applied throughout, never hidden behind fallbacks.

conops.paraphrase: When a visitor loads the page, all body and heading text renders in the Geist typeface, contributing to a polished first impression.

requirements.title: The /graph page shall render a visible typographic hierarchy in which the hero heading, section and lane headings, and side-panel body text are distinguishable by size and weight

vision.paraphrase: Clear typographic hierarchy for the hero, lane headings, and panel guides visitors through content importance and structure.

conops.paraphrase: When the page renders, text hierarchy clearly distinguishes the hero heading, lane headings, and body content by size and weight.

requirements.title: The / and /graph pages shall render surfaces from a declared palette in which the graph's folder colors serve as the interface accent colors

vision.paraphrase: A deliberate palette with folder-color accents makes the interface feel authored around its own data, fixing issue #4 finding B10.
Deliberate visual identity with a committed palette and folder-accent system ensures the interface reads as intentional, not templated.

conops.paraphrase: When a visitor loads the page, surfaces render colors from a declared palette with folder colors doubling as interface accents.

requirements.title: The /graph page shall render a visible focus indicator on every interactive control when that control receives keyboard focus

vision.paraphrase: Keyboard support with visible focus states ensures accessibility for keyboard-driven visitors.

conops.paraphrase: When a visitor tabs through interactive controls, each control renders a visible focus indicator upon receiving keyboard focus.

requirements.title: The Color theme section shall display 3 curated font+accent-color presets in addition to the existing light/dark toggle

vision.paraphrase: The theme chooser extends the existing dark/light toggle with 3 pre-validated font and accent-color combinations chosen via curated swatches.
The theme chooser surface shows the existing light/dark toggle alongside curated preset swatches offering alternative font and accent pairings.

conops.paraphrase: When a visitor opens the Options & help popover, the Color theme section displays both the light/dark toggle and 3 preset swatches representing distinct visual identities.

requirements.title: Selecting a curated theme preset shall update both the page's chrome and the graph's node color palette to that preset's validated values

vision.paraphrase: Picking a curated preset re-themes both chrome and the graph's node palette in sync, maintaining the existing design affordance where these two color systems are coupled.

conops.paraphrase: When a visitor clicks a preset swatch, the page's font pairing and header/button/focus-ring colors update immediately, and the graph's categorical node palette updates to the same preset's validated scheme.

requirements.title: The Color theme section shall provide a 4th 'Custom' option that reveals a color picker for selecting an arbitrary accent color

vision.paraphrase: A 4th 'Custom' option lets visitors pick their own accent color via a color picker, offering personal choice beyond the curated set.

conops.paraphrase: When a visitor selects the Custom option, a color picker control becomes available for entering an arbitrary accent color value.

requirements.title: Selecting a custom accent color shall re-theme only chrome elements, leaving the graph's node color palette unchanged

vision.paraphrase: The custom option is chrome-only: a visitor-chosen color updates header/button/focus styling but is not re-validated into the categorical node palette, breaking the sync intentionally.

conops.paraphrase: When a visitor picks a custom color, chrome elements (header, buttons, focus ring) update to that color, but the graph's node palette remains on its current preset or custom scheme.

requirements.title: The theme chooser shall visibly disclose that a custom accent color is not validated for CVD-safety or contrast, distinguishing it from the curated presets

vision.paraphrase: The UI must disclose that a visitor-chosen custom accent has not been validated for color-vision-deficiency safety, unlike the pre-validated curated presets.

conops.paraphrase: When a custom color is selected, a visible note informs the visitor that the chosen color is not validated for accessibility guarantees the way curated presets are.
The Operational Constraints (§8) mandate that custom-theme accessibility be visibly disclosed rather than implied to match the presets' validation rigor.

requirements.title: The visitor's selected theme preset or custom color choice shall persist across page reloads via localStorage

vision.paraphrase: Selection persists via localStorage, matching the same pattern used for the existing dark/light theme preference.

conops.paraphrase: When a visitor reloads the page after selecting a preset or custom color, the previously chosen theme is restored without requiring re-selection.

requirements.title: Switching from a custom accent color back to a curated preset shall re-sync both chrome and the graph's node color palette to that preset's validated values

vision.paraphrase: Picking a curated preset re-themes both chrome and graph palette together, re-establishing the validated sync that the custom option temporarily breaks.

conops.paraphrase: When a visitor switches from a custom accent back to a curated preset, both chrome and the graph's node palette update together to that preset's validated color scheme.
